sources.entry: Learn Claude Code by shareAI-lab - A really interesting analysis of how coding agents like Claude Code are designed. It attempts to break an agent down into its fundamental parts and reconstruct it with minimal code. Great learning resource. Final product is a rudimentary agent with skills, sub-agents, and a todo-list in roughly a few hundred lines of Python.

summary.one_liner: A 17-lesson tutorial course that rebuilds the core "harness" mechanisms behind coding agents like Claude Code (agent loop, tools, permissions, hooks, skills, subagents, tasks, teams, MCP) as small runnable Python files.
summary.what_it_does: The repository is a progressive course organized as folders s01 through s17, each with an English README (plus Chinese and Japanese translations), a standalone code.py, and SVG diagrams where needed. Each lesson isolates one harness mechanism around a core agent loop: tool use via a dispatch map, a permission approval pipeline, pre/post tool hooks, TodoWrite-style planning, subagents with fresh message lists, on-demand skill loading, context compaction, memory, a file-backed task graph, background threads, cron scheduling, multi-agent teams with worktrees, MCP tool pooling, a workflow runtime, and a goal loop that gates stopping. A legacy 12-lesson track under docs/ and agents/ is kept for older links. The README also includes a web app that presents the course and points to two related projects (Kode CLI and kode-agent-sdk) and a sister tutorial, claw0, for always-on assistants.
use_cases: learn how coding agents like Claude Code are structured internally
build a minimal agent loop with tool calling
understand agent permissions, hooks, and context compaction
implement subagents, skills, and a todo planning step in Python
study multi-agent coordination with task graphs and worktrees
follow a step-by-step harness engineering course
how_to_run: git clone the repository (URL not preserved in the README text)
cd web && npm install && npm run dev  # optional web platform
notable: Each lesson is a standalone runnable code.py that adds one mechanism to a shared agent loop
Explicit framing that the model supplies agency while the surrounding code is the harness
Includes a legacy-to-current mapping table between the 12-lesson and 17-lesson tracks
Ends with a goal loop where an independent evaluator decides whether the agent may stop
caveats: Requires an Anthropic API key (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) to run the lessons
Two chapter numbering schemes (legacy 12-lesson and current 17-lesson) can be confusing when mixed
The README's clone URL is missing from the provided text, so exact clone steps must be taken from the repository itself
